prompt: A clean a physics ray diagram of light entering GLASS: a red incident ray and a blue refracted ray bending into the tinted glass below a flat surface line. The bend must obey Snell's law: the sine of the angle of incidence divided by the sine of the angle of refraction (both measured from the surface normal) must equal the index n = 1.5. The refracted (blue) ray must bend TOWARD the normal by exactly the Snell amount. Do NOT under-bend or over-bend the refracted ray. Plain background, no numbers.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a physics ray diagram of light entering GLASS: a red incident ray and a blue refracted ray bending into the tinted glass below a flat surface line. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image show a red ray above a surface line and a blue ray below it, meeting at the surface? Answer NO only if those are missing or it is unrelated. yes or no.

reference.q_notext: Is there any printed number or written measurement note anywhere in this diagram? Answer yes or no.

steps.target: RED incident ray -- the bold straight red line in the air above the flat surface, drawn from its far tip down to the spot where it meets that surface line
